title: Winchester VA - ALPR contracts, policies, and logs

communications.subject: Virginia Freedom of Information Act Request: Winchester VA - ALPR contracts, policies, and logs
communications.communication:
November 16, 2026
Lieutenant Michael Ackerman 
Winchester Police Department
Re: Freedom of Information Act Request - ALPR contracts, policies, and logs

Pursuant to the Virginia Freedom of Information Act § 2.2-3700., I request copies of the following public records maintained by the Winchester Police Department.

Herein the term “ALPR” refers to both License Plate Reader (LPR) and Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) technology.

1. All contracts, purchase orders, or agreements between the department and Axon Enterprise, Inc, or any affiliated entity, for ALPR technology, including any amendments, renewals, or statements of work. 

2. All data-sharing agreements, memoranda of understanding, or interoperability agreements between the department and any federal agency, state agency, or private entity governing access to or use of ALPR data created by the department.

3. A complete count or inventory of ALPR cameras, both fixed and mobile, currently deployed or operated by the department (regardless of manufacturer and vendor), including location and installation date for each.

4. All written policies, procedures, general orders, or directives governing the use, access, retention, and auditing of ALPR data by department personnel, including any policies on sharing data with outside agencies.

5. All audit logs, access logs, or query records reflecting searches of the ALPR system conducted by department personnel or by outside agencies with access, including the identity of the querying officer or agency, the queried plate or hotlist, and the stated reason for the search where recorded.

For each item, the period covered is November 1, 2025 through present.

Please produce records in electronic format, native where feasible. For item 5, please produce the audit and query records as a native electronic export from the system, in CSV or Excel, rather than as a printout or a summary.

I ask that fees be reduced or waived under § 2.2-3704. The primary purpose of this request is to disseminate the information to the general public, and it is not for commercial use. If the estimated fee will exceed $25.00, please send me an itemized estimate before you begin processing. To the extent any portion of a record is exempt, please release the non-exempt portions and identify the specific exemption claimed for anything withheld, as § 2.2-3704.01 requires. If no records exist, please provide a written certification rather than leaving the item unanswered. Please deliver records electronically via email. 

Virginia FOIA requires a response within five business days of receipt, with one possible extension of seven business days upon written notice stating the reason.

If any part of this request is unclear, please tell me in writing and I will work with you on it.

Sincerely,

Mathew James
103 Winton Lane
Stephens City VA 22655

To Whom It May Concern:

The Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) is submitting this request for records under the California Public Records Act related to the acquisition and cost of services and devices provided by Axon and any of its subsidiaries and partners. 

*Background*
Axon (also known as Axon Enterprise, Inc.) is a company that describes itself as providing “public safety technology solutions” to a variety of customers, many of which are law enforcement agencies based in the United States. For reference, Axon’s website is www.axon.com. These “solutions” may be equipment, software, or “artificial intelligence”-driven analysis of video and data. Some examples of equipment, software, and services created and sold by Axon include (but are not limited to):
• the TASER, a conducted energy device
• body-worn cameras (often referred to as “Axon Body”)
• Axon Fusus, a platform used to integrate cameras and other data into a “real-time crime center” (RTCC) 
• Axon 911, an AI-driven assistant platform for dispatchers
• Axon Evidence, a platform to integrate evidence and other information
• Axon Outpost, an automated license plate reader (ALPR) system
• Axon Lightpost, an ALPR system designed for integration with streetlights
• the Axon AI Era Plan, a collection of AI-driven analysis software (www.axon.com/products/axon-ai-era-plan)
• Axon Vision, an AI-driven video analysis system
• Axon Assistant, an AI-driven chatbot
• Axon Draft One, an AI-assisted police report generation feature
• Axon Records, a records management system
• Axon virtual reality training
• Axon Air DFR, a drone-as-first-responder platform, which may also include drones created by a company called Skydio

Axon provides services or devices to the majority of policing agencies in the United States. Axon often “bundles” services and devices into a single contract, makes adjustments and additions to existing agreements for the provision of new goods, and is designated a “sole source provider” during the procurement process. Contracts and agreements may be active for many years and may include “escalator” clauses that describe ongoing and increasing costs for the procurement over the life of the contract.

*Timeframe*
The requested records are all those related to agreements with Axon active during the year 2026, as well as those agreements related to devices, services, and payments to be provided in the future. 

*Requested records*
This public records request is for materials related to the acquisition and cost of services and devices provided by Axon and any of its subsidiaries and partners. 

1. CONTRACT AND AGREEMENTS
All contracts, memorandums of understanding, and any other written agreements between this agency and Axon. Response records included all associated amendments, exhibits, and supplemental and supporting documentation for each agreement, including any amendments and materials generated subsequent to the initial contract agreement. If this agency uses any Axon product, including but not limited to the ones listed above, agreements referencing those products are responsive to this request; this includes all agreements related to “trial” or “free” periods of use. 

2. FINANCIAL AND PROCUREMENT MATERIALS
All relevant procurement and financial documents and agreements, as well as records of financial transactions, exchanges, and obligations relevant to devices and services procured from Axon. Some of these details and documents may be included as part of the Master Services and Purchasing Agreement or related quotes. 
Responsive materials include: 
• quote materials
• invoices and bills
• records describing specific pricing for each associated line item, including the unit price, the quantity procured of each unit, and associated pricing components. If additional products will be procured over the life of the contract, please be sure to provide records that reflect future acquisitions under the agreement and their cost. 
• receipts
• Requests for Proposal to which Axon provided a response
• bidding materials provided by Axon
• justifications for sole source designation (or equivalent designation, if different terminology is used in your jurisdiction) and associated materials. Responsive materials include any letters and drafts provided by Axon, any supporting materials provided by the company, and any related resolutions and materials generated by the jurisdiction in the process of obtaining a sole source designation for Axon. If the company is not subject to competitive purchasing procedures for a reason that is not a “sole source designation” (for example, because the agreement is part of a cooperative or collaborative purchase), please provide records sufficient to show why the company or the contract is not subject to competitive bidding. 
• records sufficient to show the projected ongoing cost of the agreement with Axon
• records reflecting any discounts or other calculations that were figured into the costs associated with this procurement

*Provision of records*
We ask that these materials be provided on a rolling basis; please provide materials to us as your office collects and reviews records. Please contact us for further discussion regarding the search and release of these materials.

*Fees*
In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform us of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. 
This request is not being made for commercial purposes. Please assess fees appropriately in accordance with a public records request being made in the public interest for research and journalism purposes.

*Format of responsive records*
I request that all records be disclosed in their native, digital format and transmitted to us electronically. 

*Contact information*
If you need any more information in order to process the request, or cannot process a portion of the request for any reason, please respond to the email address on this request or “beryl@eff.org”. Please let us know if a phone call will be necessary or desirable; such contact information will be provided upon request.

Thank you very much for your time and help.

Sincerely,
Beryl Lipton

title: FBI: World Champion Seattle Swimmer Helene Emma Madison

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FBI: World Champion Seattle Swimmer Helene Emma Madison
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, I request copies of all records concerning Helene Emma Madison (deceased) maintained by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, including Headquarters, the Seattle Field Office, and the Los Angeles Field Office. This includes main files, cross-references, memoranda, correspondence, indices, and electronic surveillance (ELSUR) records, for the period 1913 to the present.

1. Subject Identifying Information

• Full name: Helene Emma Madison
• Name variants: Helene Madison McIver; Helene McIver; Mrs. Lyle McIver; Helene Madison Artur (or Arthur); Helen Madison; Madison, Helene
• Date of birth: June 19, 1913
• Place of birth: Madison, Wisconsin
• Date of death: November 27, 1970 (some sources give November 25, 1970)
• Place of death: Seattle, Washington
• Residences: Seattle, Washington (Green Lake / North Seattle, including 6612 Sunnyside Ave. N.); Los Angeles / Hollywood, California (circa 1932–1933)
• Occupations and affiliations: 1932 U.S. Olympic gold medalist in swimming; swimmer with Seattle's Crystal Pool and the Washington Athletic Club under coach Ray Daughters; actress in The Human Fish (1932) and The Warrior's Husband (1933); swimming instructor (Moore Pool; Helene Madison Swim School); nurse in Seattle

2. Proof of Death

Ms. Madison died in Seattle in November 1970. Numerous civic institutions and organization written biographies that describe her life and sad death. Including the Washington Athletic Club's website:

https://www.wac.net/wac-wire/queen-helene-madison/#:~:text=But%20I%20placed%20third.%E2%80%9D%20Asked%20if%20she,used%20to%20start%20her%20Olympic%20medal%20races. 

In addition, her date of birth is more than 100 years before the date of this request, so she is presumed deceased under DOJ and FBI FOIA practice. Because her death is established, I ask that the FBI not issue a Glomar response and that it process this request on the basis that any personal privacy interest of the subject is diminished. I understand that names and identifying details of living third parties may still be protected under 5 U.S.C. § 552(b)(6) and (b)(7)(C), and I do not seek to challenge those redactions where they properly apply.

3. Scope of Search

Please search the Central Records System, the Universal Index, the ELSUR Index, and all manual, legacy, and field-office indices at HQ, Seattle, and Los Angeles, under all names listed above and reasonable spelling variants. Please locate both main files and cross-references ("see" references) in which Ms. Madison is named or mentioned, including in files concerning:

• The 1932 Summer Olympic Games in Los Angeles, California
• The Washington Athletic Club or Seattle swimming and athletic associations (circa 1928–1965)
• Professional swimming, exhibition, or touring engagements following her 1932 Olympic victories
• Motion picture studios or productions in which she appeared (1932–1933)
• Threats, extortion, harassment, or other matters in which she was a victim, complainant, or witness
• Background investigations, security clearances, or loyalty checks in which she was interviewed as a reference, neighbor, acquaintance, or spouse
• Correspondence (either to or from) Director J. Edgar Hoover where she is mentioned either in passing or as a focus of bureau investigation or interest. 

If any responsive records have been transferred to the National Archives and Records Administration, please identify them and their location. If any have been destroyed, please provide the disposition information.

Please also include a search of any records or documents understood to be, or colloquially referred to as, "COINTELPRO records" under the bureau's custody that could be construed as responsive to a request for records related to Helene Madison. 

According to a blog post read, it is important that I state the following: "As you know, the Federal Bureau of Investigation is required to search the records stored at NARA’s Washington Records Center in Suitland, MD, but still technically under the FBI’s control. For more information see 36 CFR 1250.8" Please also conduct a physical search of records at NARA's Washington Records Center in Suitland, for any records or documents related to Helene Madison. 

Thank you for the work the bureau does every day, and thank you for the bureau's commitment to transparency.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware
